# Faktra — فكترة

> E-invoicing and accounting software for businesses in the United Arab
> Emirates and Egypt. In the UAE it generates, validates and archives PINT
> AE invoices and computes UAE VAT including Designated Zone rules, the
> profit margin scheme and excise tax. In Egypt it builds, serialises,
> seals and submits the Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoice and e-receipt,
> and computes VAT at 14%. Both markets share accounting, stock,
> purchasing, collections, payroll and twelve sector modules. Available in
> Arabic and English. Last updated: 2026-09-11.

Faktra is a multi-tenant web application. It is **not** an accredited
service provider (ASP). In the UAE it produces and validates the PINT AE
file, and official reporting is transmitted through an accredited provider
that the customer appoints and the system connects to. Any claim that
Faktra reports to the UAE authority on its own would be false.

Egypt works differently, and the difference is structural rather than a
matter of wording: **Egypt has no accredited provider between the taxpayer
and the authority.** The taxpayer submits directly, under credentials the
authority issues in their own name, and Faktra performs that submission on
their behalf using those credentials. The regime a company falls under is
determined by its country, once, in the data — not by a setting somebody
can get wrong.

## Key facts

- **Markets**: United Arab Emirates (prices in AED) and Egypt (prices in
  EGP). The system decides format, tax rate and reporting route from the
  company's country.
- **Languages**: Arabic and English, on separate URLs (`/ar/`, `/en/`).
  Country is a switch within each language, not a separate URL.
- **Plans, UAE**: Starter AED 199/month, Business AED 499/month,
  Professional AED 899/month.
- **Plans, Egypt**: Starter EGP 899/month, Business EGP 1,999/month,
  Professional EGP 3,999/month.
- Annual billing gives two months free in both markets.
- **Trial**: 14 days, no payment card required.
- **User limits**: 3, 10 and 25 users respectively.

## Egypt: the e-invoice and e-receipt

- The regime is **already in force**, in phases that have finished — it is
  not an upcoming deadline. A paper invoice today is outside a live rule.
- **VAT** general rate is 14%. Tax registration numbers are nine digits.
- The **e-receipt is a separate track** from the invoice, not a flag on
  one: receipts are batched, and a single seal covers a whole batch rather
  than each receipt.
- **Serialisation is exact.** The authority verifies the seal against a
  canonical string, so a value written as `14.00` must not be emitted as
  `14`. Equal numbers, invalid document.
- The **sealing certificate lives on a hardware token in the taxpayer's
  own office**. No server can hold it, so a small local agent on that
  machine receives the canonical string and signs it. Faktra does not hold
  customer signing keys.
- Faktra **refuses before issue, not after**: an item with no code, a
  company with no activity code, a party with no registration number, or a
  credit note with no original invoice. An issued invoice already carries
  a legal number and a ledger entry, so a later rejection costs a credit
  note rather than a correction.

## UAE e-invoicing timeline

Under UAE Ministerial Decisions 243 and 244 of 2025:

- 1 July 2026 — voluntary onboarding opens
- 30 October 2026 — ASP appointment deadline, turnover ≥ AED 50m
- 1 January 2027 — mandatory reporting begins, large businesses
- 31 March 2027 — ASP appointment deadline, turnover < AED 50m
- 1 July 2027 — reporting begins for remaining businesses

Verify these against the Ministry of Finance before relying on them.

## Worked examples that distinguish the product

- **Profit margin scheme**: a used car bought for AED 56,000 and sold for
  AED 60,000 has a margin of AED 4,000. VAT is 5/105 of that margin =
  AED 190.48, not 5% of 60,000. Charging the full rate overcharges the
  buyer by AED 2,809 per vehicle.
- **Designated Zones**: selling into a Designated Zone is not an export;
  the company there is a UAE company and the supply is standard rated.
  The rule covers goods, not services.
- **Excise tax**: computed on the published retail price, not on cost or
  selling price. 1,000 energy drinks at a published price of AED 12 at
  100% = AED 12,000 due, less deductions for re-exports.
- **Manufacturing**: a run of 20 chairs yielding 18 divides the whole run
  cost by 18, not by 20. Dividing by the planned quantity undervalues
  stock and overstates margin on every later sale.
- **Post-dated cheques**: a cheque settles the invoice on the day it is
  handed over while the bank balance moves only when it clears, so the
  customer is not chased and the money is not spent early.

## Integrity checks built into the product

Four figures whose only acceptable value is zero, computed against the
customer's own data: tenant isolation violations, stock value versus the
Inventory ledger account, customer and supplier balances versus their
control accounts, and unbalanced journal entries.
